98bef07f09.q: What is the Food Innovation Center in Green Bay and what amenities does it offer to farmers?
98bef07f09.a: The Food Innovation Center is a 3,500 square foot facility being built on the JBS development site in Green Bay's east side, opening early next year. It features an outside pack wash station, irrigation line, cold storage, walk-in freezer and cooler, dry storage space, and a 1,500 square foot processing facility. The facility was designed based on what farmers identified they were lacking, with potential to expand across four to seven additional acres of land if needed in the future.

86da934bab.q: Why do small-scale farmers in Northeast Wisconsin lose produce at the end of the growing season?
86da934bab.a: Farmers markets in Northeast Wisconsin only operate for five to six months at most, and once that season ends, farmers still have harvestable crops. Most of this produce either goes to compost for the next year, gets tilled over, or becomes animal feed, representing significant waste that could otherwise feed families through value-added processing.

e9a9455c81.q: What is the JBS neighborhood development project in Green Bay and how large is it?
e9a9455c81.a: The JBS development is one of the largest developments the city of Green Bay has ever undertaken, built on about 26 and a half acres of land that was donated by JBS, the meat company. It includes public spaces and a public park, roads connecting under-resourced neighborhoods like Imperial Pride, the Food Innovation Center, and both market rate and affordable housing.

c76b04dc82.q: How will the Food Innovation Center serve as a workforce training ground for agriculture and food manufacturing careers?
c76b04dc82.a: The facility uses specialized but small-scale industrial equipment, allowing farmers and young professionals to gain transferable skills in sanitation, standard operating procedures, and food manufacturing. These skills enable participants to either scale their own businesses or transition into larger food manufacturing companies with established expertise, while also helping farmers with decades of institutional knowledge apply their skills across different sectors of the agriculture industry.

d040838a07.q: Who are the main partners supporting the Food Innovation Center project in Green Bay?
d040838a07.a: The two major partners are the City of Green Bay, Wello, and Oneida Nation, who helped close the funding gap for construction. Additional partners include New North, University of Wisconsin-Green Bay, NWTC, and Green Bay Area Public School Districts, which has an agricultural program and wants to involve its youth in the facility's programming.
